record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: Let A be the set of all symmetric idempotent matrices on the real vector space R^n; that is, for every A in A, AA = A. Let I be the identity matrix and 0 the zero matrix. A fuzzy relation s: A x A -> [0, 1] is an s-map if s(I, I) = 1; if A, B in A satisfy AB = BA = 0 then s(A, B) = 0; and if A, B in A satisfy AB = BA = 0, then for every C in A, s(A + B, C) = s(A, C) + s(B, C) and s(C, A + B) = s(C, A) + s(C, B). Must every such s-map be symmetric, meaning s(A, B) = s(B, A) for all A, B in A?

evidence.quote: Let A be the set of all symmetric matrices defined on the real vector space R^n, such that for each A in A we have AA = A.
A fuzzy relation s : A x A -> [0, 1] is called an s-map if (i) s(I, I) = 1.
Problem 10.1. Is the fuzzy relation s necessarily symmetric, i.e., s(A, B) = s(B, A) for all A, B in A?

artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 paper in Kybernetika proves that s-maps are symmetric fuzzy relations on the set of all symmetric and idempotent binary matrices, which the authors describe as solving a problem proposed at FSTA 2006. This resolves the binary-matrix case affirmatively, but the original question over real symmetric idempotent matrices in $\mathbb{R}^n$ does not appear to be fully settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Properties of quantum logic maps as fuzzy relations on a set of symmetric and idempotent binary matrices
status_evidence.snippet: it is proved that s-maps are symmetric fuzzy relations on a set of all symmetric and idempotent binary matrices. Consequently s-maps are not antisymmetric fuzzy relations.
status_evidence.claim: The symmetry of s-maps is established for symmetric idempotent binary matrices, addressing the FSTA problem in that setting.
